summary: This bill reauthorizes the Weatherization Assistance Program, increasing the maximum average cost per dwelling unit for weatherization projects from $6,500 to $12,000, and mandates a report on the impact of enhancement and innovation readiness efforts on program eligibility.

scores.thoughts: This bill reauthorizes the Weatherization Assistance Program and increases its funding levels significantly over several fiscal years, directly leading to more government spending.

The bill focuses on weatherization, which improves energy efficiency in homes. This directly contributes to reducing energy consumption and, consequently, greenhouse gas emissions, thus promoting environmental protection.

The bill directly reauthorizes and increases funding for the Weatherization Assistance Program, raising the per-unit cap from $6,500 to $12,000 and authorizing $300–350 million annually through FY2030 with no offsets or revenue provisions. This constitutes new federal spending authority whose primary effect is to enlarge the deficit to fund program expansion.
